prompts.display_text: Pin an Oceania country or territory (Hawaii counts as USA) where Latter-day Saint missionaries preached before 1900.
prompts.text_original: Before 1900, Latter-day Saint missionaries had preached in only a handful of Pacific island lands and Australia. Pin a country or territory where, according to the Church Global Histories, they preached before 1900.
prompts.note: USA is scored for Hawaii. Fiji's first known member arrived in 1924, so Fiji is not scored.
prompts.summary: The Church reached the Pacific early: Addison Pratt landed in the Austral Islands in 1844, missionaries reached Hawaii in 1850 and New Zealand in 1854. Hawaiian missionaries carried the gospel to Samoa in 1863, and Tonga opened in 1891. Fiji, Guam and the Micronesian islands came only in the 20th century.

answers.name: Australia
answers.fact: Ordained convert William Barratt reached Adelaide in 1840 and baptized the first Australian in 1842.

answers.name: New Zealand
answers.fact: Augustus Farnham and William Cooke reached Auckland in October 1854.

answers.name: French Polynesia
answers.fact: Addison Pratt arrived at Tubuai in the Austral Islands in April 1844.

answers.name: Tonga
answers.fact: First Church meeting held at Pea, Tongatapu, in August 1891.

answers.name: United States
answers.fact: Hawaii: first missionaries arrived in 1850; 50th anniversary marked in 1900.

answers.name: Samoa
answers.fact: Samoan Mission opened 1888; Ifopa baptized on Upolu in 1889.

answers.name: American Samoa
answers.fact: Kimo Pelio and Samuela Manoa preached on Aunuu from 1863; Deans arrived 1888.

answers.name: Cook Islands
answers.fact: Missionaries made occasional visits, as at Mangaia, between 1845 and 1899.

prompts.display_text: Pin a country whose modern name, or its main word, appears as a land, river or people in the King James New Testament
prompts.text_original: A present-day country whose name, or the main word of it, is spelled as a land, river or people in the King James New Testament
prompts.note: This prompt is about the name only, so Malta (Melita) and Romania (Romans) do not count.
prompts.summary: A dozen modern countries carry a name the King James New Testament already uses. Egypt, Israel, Syria, Greece, Italy and Cyprus are familiar, and the nation of Jordan takes its name from the river. Arabia, Macedonia, the Ethiopians, Libya and Spain also appear, the last as the place Paul hoped to reach after Rome.

answers.name: Egypt
answers.fact: Joseph was told to flee into Egypt (Matthew 2:13).

answers.name: Israel
answers.fact: Joseph was told to go into the land of Israel (Matthew 2:20).

answers.name: Greece
answers.fact: Paul came into Greece and stayed three months (Acts 20:2-3).

answers.name: Italy
answers.fact: It was determined that Paul should sail into Italy (Acts 27:1).

answers.name: Syria
answers.fact: Jesus' fame went throughout all Syria (Matthew 4:24).

answers.name: Cyprus
answers.fact: Barnabas was a Levite of the country of Cyprus (Acts 4:36).

answers.name: Jordan
answers.fact: John baptized in Jordan; the country takes its name from the river (Matthew 3:6).

answers.name: Ethiopia
answers.fact: Philip met a eunuch of great authority under Candace, queen of the Ethiopians (Acts 8:27).

answers.name: North Macedonia
answers.fact: Paul saw a man of Macedonia in a vision (Acts 16:9).

answers.name: Saudi Arabia
answers.fact: Paul went into Arabia after his conversion; Arabians heard at Pentecost (Galatians 1:17; Acts 2:11).

answers.name: Spain
answers.fact: Paul hoped to visit the Romans whenever he took his journey into Spain (Romans 15:24).

answers.name: Libya
answers.fact: Pentecost pilgrims came from the parts of Libya about Cyrene (Acts 2:10).

prompts.display_text: Pin one of the 5 Asian countries Church History Topics names where servicemembers helped introduce the Church after World War II.
prompts.text_original: After World War II, Latter-day Saint servicemembers helped introduce or reestablish the Church in Asian countries where they were stationed. Pin one of the countries Church History Topics names.
prompts.citation: Church History Topics: Globalization; Growth of Missionary Work
prompts.summary: Church History Topics credits American Latter-day Saint servicemembers stationed abroad after World War II with helping introduce or reestablish the Church, especially in Japan, Korea, the Philippines, Vietnam and Thailand. Their servicemen's groups often grew into the first local branches.

answers.name: Japan
answers.fact: Named; servicemembers met in postwar Japan (Saints vol. 3 ch. 31).

answers.name: South Korea
answers.fact: Named; Korean War servicemen helped plant the Church.

answers.name: Philippines
answers.fact: Named; servicemen met in the Philippines after the war.

answers.name: Thailand
answers.fact: Named among countries where servicemembers helped establish the Church.

answers.name: Vietnam
answers.fact: Named; servicemember groups met there during the Vietnam War.
